text: Start where most people actually start — someone sent you a link. Paste a raw deck I.D. and NodeSlide refuses it. This is an editor link, not a share link. Raw deck I.D.s do not grant access. You need the private recovery key, a deck this browser already owns, or a view-only presentation link.

Now the developer's door. Connect your own runtime — use your provider without giving NodeSlide the key. Values live in this tab's session storage and run in a local process you launch. They are never sent to the backend, never written into Trace, and never returned by a tool.

The other half of that panel lets Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor drive NodeSlide directly. An agent can read decks and traces, upload evidence, and propose edits — and proposals stay unapplied until a separate accept call. Same locks, second front door.
For anyone asking whether the output quality is real, there is the Artifact Lab — thirty-eight evidence-bound recipes, with route comparison and export receipts.

Every card carries its own evidence: source J.SON, a trace, and an export receipt. Even the headline number stays tied to a frozen receipt — eighty-two of eighty-four candidates cleared browser and PowerPoint proof — instead of becoming marketing shorthand.
When the deck is ready, it presents. Full screen, speaker notes one key away, seven slides of the same structured content you have been editing.
And it leaves. Interactive H.T.M.L. — a web-native deck with notes — or PowerPoint, as editable P.P.T.X. with fallbacks. The structure survives the trip out.
Refused safely, connected on your terms, evidenced, presented, exported. Five doors, one system.
